August 27, 2026·14 min read

Lumentum · Optical networking · AI infrastructure · Financial analysis · Scenario analysis

# [Financial Analysis of Lumentum, August 2026](#financial-analysis-of-lumentum-august-2026)

**Lumentum has finished converting itself from a cyclical telecom-component supplier into an AI-infrastructure supplier, and fiscal 2026 is the year the numbers prove it.** Revenue rose 83.2% to $3,014.0m, GAAP operating margin swung from −10.9% to +17.4%, and free cash flow turned positive at $300.1m after two years of burn. The exit rate matters more than the year: fourth-quarter revenue was $1,006.3m at a 36.6% non-GAAP operating margin, and the first quarter of fiscal 2027 is guided to $1.225–1.275bn at 39.5–40.5%.

**The $6,935.1m GAAP net loss is not an operating event.** It is a $7,756.6m non-cash charge from settling $1,124.9m of convertible principal in stock while the share price sat far above the conversion prices. It consumed no cash, it moved $10,443.3m into paid-in capital, and it took equity from $1,134.7m to $4,643.9m and net debt of $1,696.1m to net cash of $1,101.0m.

**The risk has moved from the balance sheet to the customer list.** Two customers are 41.6% of revenue and one is 30.4% of receivables, in the most capital-cycle-sensitive spending line in technology — and Lumentum has just fixed $1,159.1m of property and equipment against it.

## [1. Where the business stands](#1-where-the-business-stands)

Lumentum makes the optical and photonic parts that move data inside and between data centres: semiconductor laser chips, laser sub-assemblies, wavelength management systems, optical modules, optical circuit switches and industrial lasers. Fiscal 2026 ended 27 June 2026. From the first quarter of that year the company retired its two reportable segments — Cloud & Networking and Industrial Tech — and now reports as a single enterprise, with prior periods recast. What remains is a disaggregation by product type.

| $ millions        | FY2024  | FY2025  | FY2026  | y/y    | % of FY26 |
| ----------------- | ------- | ------- | ------- | ------ | --------- |
| Components        | 822.1   | 1,116.3 | 2,005.6 | +79.7% | 66.5%     |
| Systems           | 537.1   | 528.7   | 1,008.4 | +90.7% | 33.5%     |
| Total net revenue | 1,359.2 | 1,645.0 | 3,014.0 | +83.2% | 100.0%    |

The quarterly path is the part worth memorising, because the annual figure understates where the business exited.

| Quarter          | Revenue FY26 | Revenue FY25 | y/y     | GAAP gross margin | GAAP operating margin | Non-GAAP gross margin | Non-GAAP operating margin | Non-GAAP EPS |
| ---------------- | ------------ | ------------ | ------- | ----------------- | --------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------ |
| Q1               | 533.8        | 336.9        | +58.4%  | 34.0%             | 1.3%                  | 39.4%                 | 18.7%                     | $1.10        |
| Q2               | 665.5        | 402.2        | +65.5%  | 36.1%             | 9.7%                  | 42.5%                 | 25.2%                     | $1.67        |
| Q3               | 808.4        | 425.2        | +90.1%  | 44.2%             | 21.6%                 | 47.9%                 | 32.2%                     | $2.37        |
| Q4               | 1,006.3      | 480.7        | +109.3% | 47.4%             | 27.8%                 | 50.4%                 | 36.6%                     | $3.23        |
| Q1 FY27 guidance | 1,225–1,275  | 533.8        | ~134%   | —                 | —                     | —                     | 39.5–40.5%                | $4.05–4.35   |

Q1, Q2 and Q4 of fiscal 2025 as reported in the corresponding quarterly Form 8-K exhibits. Q3 fiscal 2025 of $425.2m is derived as the residual against the reported $1,645.0m full year. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded in every quarter of fiscal 2026 — by 650bp, 700bp and 440bp sequentially after the first.

![SVG Image]

*Revenue growth and margin expansion compound into one line. Non-GAAP operating income ran $99.8m, $167.7m, $260.7m and $368.8m through fiscal 2026 — the third and fourth quarters as reported in the fiscal 2026 reconciliation, the first two derived from reported revenue and reported non-GAAP margin, and the four tie to the reported $897.0m full year. The guidance bar applies the midpoint of the 39.5–40.5% margin range to the $1.25bn revenue midpoint.*

**The guidance is the analysis.** A $1.25bn quarter annualises to $5.0bn against fiscal 2026's $3.01bn. Management said it is “reaching our target model more than a quarter ahead of schedule.” Simply holding the first-quarter rate flat for four quarters is a 66% year. Everything in the scenarios below is a question of what happens on top of that.

## [2. Twelve months of 8-K filings](#2-twelve-months-of-8-k-filings)

**Capacity is being added industry-wide, not only at Lumentum.** $2.1bn of combined capital expenditure in a single year against a combined revenue base of $20.0bn. ## [7. Critical factors driving the bull case](#7-critical-factors-driving-the-bull-case)

Six factors, ordered by how much revenue each can add and how well each is evidenced in the filings rather than in commentary.

1. **Optical circuit switches — the largest disclosed and least contested opportunity.** highest conviction  
   Backlog was stated as “well beyond $400 million” in the February 2026 8-K, against full-year Systems revenue of $1,008.4m. Management named optical circuit switches first among growth drivers in the fourth-quarter release and described “scaling rapidly to meet extraordinary customer demand.” Neither Coherent nor Fabrinet reports a competing line.
2. **Co-packaged optics laser sources.** high conviction, timing risk  
   An “incremental multi-hundred-million-dollar order” deliverable in the first half of calendar 2027 was disclosed in February 2026. The fourth-quarter release added “increasing demand for ultra-high-power CPO lasers” and an initial order for external laser source modules. Co-packaged optics moves optics inside the rack, a step change in units per accelerator, and the ultra-high-power laser is the component few others can build.
3. **1.6T cloud transceiver modules.**  
   Called out as “advancing 1.6T adoption.” This is the highest-volume and most contested part of the opportunity — Coherent, Fabrinet's customers and the Chinese module vendors all compete here — and therefore the part most likely to carry sector-average rather than premium margin.
4. **Vertical integration into the chip.**  
   Components grew 79.7% and reached 66.5% of revenue while contract-manufacturer purchase concentration fell from 25.1% to 18.2%. Lumentum is capturing more of the value in each module. This is the mechanism behind the 1,370bp of gross-margin expansion, and it has further to run.
5. **Capacity already in the ground.**  
   Property and equipment rose 59.6% to $1,159.1m on $451.3m of capital expenditure, and inventory rose 47.1% to $691.6m. Unlike a backlog, this is money already spent. It converts to revenue if demand holds — and it is precisely the fixed cost that breaks the downside case if demand does not.
6. **The NVIDIA relationship.** strategic, not contractual revenue  
   $2.0bn of equity at $695.31 per share and a stated optics technology partnership. The direct financial effect is funding. The indirect effect is roadmap alignment with the company that sets the accelerator interconnect standard. Neither is a disclosed revenue commitment.

### [What the grids show](#what-the-grids-show)

- **Revenue and margin matter about equally, which is unusual.** Moving from $3,900m to $8,405m of revenue at a constant 34% margin adds $1,532m of operating income. Moving from a 22% to a 46% margin at a constant $8,405m adds $2,017m. In most hardware businesses volume dominates. Here the margin range itself is 24 points wide, and that width is the real finding: Lumentum's earnings are roughly as sensitive to absorption as to volume.
- **Free cash flow is resilient at the bottom.** Even the worst cell — $3,900m of revenue at a 22% operating margin — produces $513m of free cash flow, because capital expenditure falls with revenue. There is no cash-burn scenario at any plausible combination of these two variables. That is the single most important defensive fact here, and it is a direct consequence of the fiscal 2026 balance-sheet reset.
- **The base case is not the middle of the grid.** Base-case fiscal 2029 operating income of $3,446m sits in the upper-right quadrant and requires both $8.4bn of revenue and a 41% margin. Missing either one moves the outcome by roughly $500m to $900m.
- **The downside is lost growth, not losses.** Every cell except the bottom-left corner exceeds fiscal 2026's $897m of non-GAAP operating income. The bear case as modelled leaves fiscal 2029 operating income approximately flat against fiscal 2026 — three years of growth forgone rather than a return to losses.
- **The asymmetry favours the upside.** Cumulative three-year free cash flow is $5,954m in the bull case against $2,577m in the bear — a $3.4bn spread for a business that generated $300m in fiscal 2026.

## [10. What would change the view](#10-what-would-change-the-view)

Six observable things, each of which resolves before the fiscal 2029 outcome is knowable.

- **Customer concentration in the next 10-K.** The top two customers went from 31.4% to 41.6% of revenue in one year, and one holds 30.4% of receivables. If that climbs further, the revenue line becomes a derivative of two capital-expenditure budgets and the downside case gets more probable rather than less.
- **Whether optical circuit switch backlog converts on schedule.** The “well beyond $400 million” figure is the single most checkable forward disclosure the company has made. Watch whether it is restated, extended or quantified again.
- **Inventory turns against purchase obligations.** Inventory of $691.6m and $2,112.5m of purchase commitments due within twelve months, against turns of only 3.0x. A quarter in which inventory grows faster than revenue is the early signal of the fiscal 2024 pattern repeating.
- **Cash settlement of the converts.** $757.8m of early conversion requests were in hand at 14 August 2026, against $2,738.4m of cash and short-term investments. This is affordable but consumes a large share of the balance.
- **Gross margin at the next volume step.** The fourth quarter reached 50.4% non-GAAP. Whether that holds as 1.6T module volume — the most competitive part of the mix — grows faster than the proprietary lines is the cleanest test of whether the margin premium is structural.
- **Sector capacity landing.** $2.1bn of combined peer capital expenditure in one year. If pricing normalises across the group, the bull-case gross margin does not hold regardless of Lumentum's own execution.
